title: AgentMessage
description: One record on the Agent Message Bus. Append-only event written as a single JSON document on disk (one line per message in JSONL files under logs/bus/<project>/<yyyy-mm-dd>.jsonl, or workspace-wide under logs/bus/_workspace/<yyyy-mm-dd>.jsonl when no project applies). The bus is an observability and control spine, not a workflow engine: a message records that something was observed, asked, decided, advised, intervened, produced, spent, transitioned, errored, or pulsed. Producing a message never moves a job between state lanes and never starts another coding task within the same project. Routine queue movement remains owned by the application runner and RunOutcomePolicy.

schemaVersion.description: Schema version. Bumped only when a non-additive change forces readers to fork. Additive optional fields keep version 1.

id.description: Globally unique id for this message. ULID or UUID v7 are recommended so the lexical order matches creation time. Used as the canonical reference target for AgentMessage.replyToId and for artifact pointers from external streams.

createdAt.description: UTC timestamp at which the message was created. Must end in Z. Writers preserve the original timestamp on retransmit; replays use the original time, not the replay time.

participantId.description: AgentParticipant.id of the actor that produced this message. The participant record carries kind, displayName, cli, and project, so consumers do not have to repeat them on every message.

role.description: Coarse intent of the message independent of kind. actor is a deliberate utterance from a participant (user prompt, agent answer, orchestrator decision). system is generated by the runtime when something happens (lifecycle, heartbeat, error). evidence wraps an artifact reference produced as a side-effect (screenshot, log slice, finding report).

kind.description: Typed message kind. observation: a reading of system or agent state, e.g. supervisor 'no progress for 60s'. question: a prompt that expects an answer, e.g. user input or orchestrator clarification. decision: a typed ruling, e.g. orchestrator reissue, accept Done, classify heuristic. advisory: cooperative-signal record from the supervisor, severity Info/Warn/High. intervention: a pre-emptive control action invoked through the runner (CancelRun, PausePickup, ForceFail, Resume). artifact: a reference to evidence produced during the run. token-usage: a closed window of token spend attributed to this participant. lifecycle: a state transition the runtime emitted (job created, run started, run stopped, sentinel parsed, state lane moved). error: an unrecoverable failure that needs a reviewer's attention. heartbeat: liveness pulse from a long-lived participant; consumers may collapse runs of heartbeats in the UI.

severity.description: Informational severity. Even High does not by itself trigger an automatic intervention; auto-intervention is gated separately. Mirrors SupervisorSeverity so advisory bridges round-trip cleanly.

project.description: Project name as it appears in WatchPaths and ProjectRunnerStatus. Null only for workspace-wide messages emitted by the global orchestrator, system-review, or runtime startup.

jobId.description: JobInfo.Id slug if this message is scoped to a single job. Null when the message is project-wide (e.g. PausePickup) or workspace-wide.

runId.description: Stable id of the CLI invocation this message belongs to. Matches the run id used by the per-job run timeline (/api/tasks/{id}/runs). Null when the message is not bound to one specific run (e.g. lifecycle:JobCreated, supervisor PausePickup).

cliSessionId.description: Provider session id for the underlying CLI when one exists (Claude session UUID, Codex session id, Copilot session, Gemini session). Lets the system-review correlate bus messages with the on-disk session evidence.

topic.description: Short kebab-case label for advisory and decision messages, e.g. no-progress, reissue, heuristic-fallback, quota-critical. Topics map to known UI glyphs and known auto-intervention actions.

summary.description: One-line human-readable description of the message. Plain prose, no markdown, under 280 characters. The timeline shows this verbatim; longer detail belongs in payload or in a markdown-report artifact.

body.description: Optional longer text body when summary is not enough (agent answer, orchestrator giveup explanation, error stack). Plain text or restricted markdown. Heavy evidence belongs in artifacts, not here.

replyToId.description: AgentMessage.id this message answers, when applicable. Lets the participant graph render question-answer pairs and lets the system-review collapse threads.

correlationId.description: Free-form correlation key for grouping messages that belong to the same logical activity but cross participants and runs (e.g. one user request that spawned one coding run plus three supporting audits). Reusing the originating user message id is a fine default.

tokens.description: Per-message token attribution when the producer knows it. token-usage messages always set this; other kinds may set it for traceability. Aggregates across windows live in token-aggregate.schema.json, not here.

model.description: Concrete model id used for this message, e.g. claude-opus-4-7.

thinkingLevel.description: Effective reasoning / thinking level the call ran at, e.g. medium. Recorded at call time by the producer; null when the producer does not know it or the model has no level. Model and level together identify what spent the tokens.

inputIncludesCached.description: Provider semantics at capture time. True means the raw provider input counter included cache hits; persisted input is nevertheless normalized to uncached input. False means input and cache-read were reported separately. Null identifies legacy rows.

usageNormalization.description: Stable repair marker when a legacy stored row was normalized after capture, for example openai-input-includes-cached-v1.

contextWindow.description: Optional snapshot of the model's context-window state at the moment this turn completed. All fields optional; populated as the CLI surfaces them.

totalSize.description: Model context-window limit in tokens (from local model-registry, not CLI).

used.description: Everything the model loaded this turn: Claude input + cacheRead, or the raw OpenAI input counter which already included cached input.

latency.description: Wall-clock latency for the model turn this message refers to. Populated by the runner; absent on messages that did not call an LLM.

artifacts.description: Zero or more references to evidence on disk or in another structured stream. Always references; never inlined bytes. See agent-artifact-ref.schema.json.

payload.description: Kind-specific structured payload. Open object so kinds can carry typed fields without forcing a schema-version bump for each addition. By convention: lifecycle messages carry { from, to, transitionReason }; intervention messages carry { kind, pauseTtl }; error messages carry { exceptionType, source }; decision messages carry { sentinel, action, retryBudgetRemaining }; question messages carry { needsInputReason, options }. Consumers ignore unknown payload fields.

tags.description: Optional flat list of short kebab-case labels for filtering: skill ids, project tags, audit categories. Not a primary index.
